title: Zero of the intermediate section under a later stage unit
statement: In the same filtered diagram of sites and supplied colimit site as [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-site-unit-zero-detection], let eV_a identify V_j^* with V_k^* F_a^* and satisfy the displayed adjunction-unit equation. Let Fs_j be abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let phi_a : F_a^* Fs_j → Fs_k be coefficient maps, and let S be a diagram of sheaves on Q with its objects identified with V_j^*Fs_j and its arrows identified in Arrow with eV_a followed by V_k^*(phi_a). Fix j, X in F_j, z in Fs_j(X), and a : j → j'. If the limit unit of z followed by the specified identification and S(a) is zero, there are k and d : j' → k such that the unit along a, followed by phi_a and then the unit along d for Fs_j', sends z to zero. No map phi_d or composition cocycle is needed or concluded.

proof.text: Correct the source of the system arrow using hSobj and its Arrow equality hSmap, evaluate at V_j(X), and precompose by the unit. This preserves the zero equation, including its endpoint transport.

Cocone naturality gives V_j(X)=V_j'(F_a X). Compose heV with the inverse image of phi_a at these equal objects. The Arrow equality preserves the zero kernel. Naturality of the adjunction unit identifies the resulting composite with the canonical limit unit applied to w=(unit_a followed by phi_a)(z).
Apply single-sheaf colimit-site unit zero detection to Fs_j' at F_a(X) and the explicitly constructed section w. The resulting d gives the asserted composite-unit zero equation.
